newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Morgan Stanley rates FCL Paper neutral.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley rates FCL Paper neutral.

text.p: In its first report on New Zealand's Fletcher Paper, U.S. sharebroker Morgan Stanley Dean Witter has concluded the company's shares are trading near fair value after rising 25 percent since April," NZPA reported on Tuesday..
"We are initiating coverage of New Zealand-based Fletcher Challenge paper with a neutral rating and a 12 month price target of $NZ3.33 per share," the company said.
Investment positives were Fletcher paper's exposure to rising newsprint prices and its strategy of focusing on publication papers and Pacific Rim markets.
"We view Fletcher Paper's decision to focus on publications papers and the Pacific Rim markets as significant investment positives for the company."

Negatives were that the company's machines were smaller, older and less cost effective than competitors, and forecasts that the company was likely to report an operating loss in the second half to June 1997.
Morgan Stanley forecasts that Fletcher paper will report a loss of $NZ70 million in the year to June 1997, compared with the first half loss of $NZ40 million.
It is forecasting a loss of NZ6c per share in the second half of that full year to June 1997 compared with a NZ10c loss in the six months to December 1996.

The forecast assumes unchanged capacity and shipments of newsprint and specialty papers compared with the first half and that they would be sold at an average realisation of $US488 ($NZ755) per tonne.

Morgan Stanley estimated that a $US50 per tonne increase in newsprint prices adds NZ8c to the company's earnings per share. The report said that investing in New Zealand's paper and forest products sector was becoming fashionable again and it said
Fletcher Paper was one of the few multi-national publications paper companies in the world today.

Fletcher Paper has six main subsidiaries -- its 50.8 percent stake in Fletcher Canada, and its majority ownership of UK Papers plc, Tasman Pulp and Paper, Australian Newsprint Mills, Papel de Impresena SA in Brazil and Papelas Bio Bio in Chile.
The report said there were signs of a stronger than expected recovery in newsprint prices.

"A major surprise in newsprint markets this year is that mills have operated flat out yet inventories have not ballooned at either mill level or publisher level. This was due to strong demand in the United States."
The valuation for Fletcher Paper shares assumes a mid cycle newsprint price of $US613 per tonne.
The report said the market for pulp was also tightening, reflecting a build up in inventories.
Three large U.S. suppliers have announced price increases of $US50 per tonne for market pulp, effective July 1, bringing the list price to $US630 per tonne.

"While the outlook for product prices has improved, we believe the stock (Fletcher paper) is fairly valued at the current price of $NZ3.46, having rallied 25 percent since early April," Morgan Stanley said.
Fletcher paper closed on Monday at $NZ3.38, down 5 cents.
